item.title: Deploying Jekyll Chirpy on GitHub Pages: The Complete Setup, CI/CD Pipeline, and Bug-Fix Playbook
item.description:
Setting up a documentation portal or department blog using the Jekyll Chirpy theme on GitHub Pages looks effortless on paper. You fork the starter repo, point GitHub Actions to your branch, and watch the site spin up.

In reality, running a production-grade Chirpy setup with custom CI/CD pipelines quickly runs into a minefield of build-time failures: Ruby Liquid crashes over integer tags, htmlproofer throwing hundreds of false-positive 404s on dynamic taxonomy routes, missing local layout overrides, broken anchor fragment checks, and invisible non-breaking spaces that crash YAML parsers.

item.title: Docker: Complete Beginner to Production Guide
item.description:
Docker: Complete Beginner to Production Guide

Docker changed software development by making applications portable and predictable. Instead of saying, “It works on my machine,” developers can package an application with everything it needs—code, libraries, runtime, and dependencies—into a container that runs consistently anywhere.

Docker has become a standard tool for developers, DevOps engineers, cloud engineers, and platform teams.

In this guide, you’ll learn Docker from the ground up and build production-ready containerized applications.

Python has become the language of choice for automation, cloud engineering, DevOps, data processing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and backend development.

item.title: Building OCR2MD: From a Simple OCR Script to a Production-Ready OCR-to-Markdown Platform
item.description:
Building OCR2MD: A Complete OCR-to-Markdown Platform

Modern organizations deal with thousands of scanned documents every year. Reports, invoices, audit records, government files, historical archives, handwritten forms, meeting notes, and books often exist only as scanned PDFs or images.

Extracting this information into a structured format is surprisingly difficult.

Most OCR tools only recover plain text. Tables lose their structure, headings become paragraphs, images disappear, and manually cleaning the results consumes far more time than the OCR itself.

item.title: Mastering PDF to Markdown on Linux Mint: A Step-by-Step Guide with Marker & MarkItDown
item.description:
Mastering PDF to Markdown on Linux Mint: A Step-by-Step Guide with Marker & MarkItDown

Converting document formats—specifically turning static, layout-heavy PDFs into clean, versatile Markdown files—is a cornerstone workflow for developers, researchers, technical writers, and knowledge management enthusiasts. Whether you are building a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline for LLMs, migrating documentation, or organizing your personal knowledge base in tools like Obsidian or Logseq, high-quality document conversion is vital.

In this comprehensive guide, we will walk through setting up two of the most powerful open-source PDF-to-Markdown tools—Marker and Microsoft’s MarkItDown—on Linux Mint (and other Ubuntu/Debian-based Linux distributions). We will cover fundamental Linux package management, navigating Python’s modern PEP 668 safety constraints, system-level dependencies like FFmpeg, and when to choose each tool based on your specific document processing needs.

item.title: Troubleshooting Python, Pip, and Path Issues on Windows: A Step-by-Step Recovery Guide
item.description:
Setting up Python tools on Windows using the Microsoft Store distribution can sometimes feel like navigating a minefield of system path warnings, ghost directories, permission locks, and version conflicts.

This guide compiles a step-by-step resolution process for real-world terminal errors encounterable when managing CLI tools like weasyprint and marker, fixing corrupted package installs, and updating dependencies without getting stuck.
